title: A raw read of a kb article for a lookup is steered to the rag.py tools
goal: A PreToolUse hook on Bash commands that read kb/public/**/*.md or a root's _gaps.md whole (cat, sed -n, head, tail, grep -n) adds context naming rag.py show, facts, audit and search --index, without blocking the read, and stays silent on every other command

gates.question: How are lookup reads of whole kb files steered to the rag.py tools?
options: a PreToolUse hook that adds context and lets the read run
a PreToolUse hook that asks before the read
the AGENTS.md rule alone, which already exists
gates.recommendation: a PreToolUse hook that adds context and lets the read run

notes: Baseline census: tool results of 314 transcripts of this project (52 sessions, 262 subagent runs), about 4 characters a token; each result is also re-read from cache on every later turn of its session. sed -n/cat/grep -n over whole articles and _gaps.md: about 750k characters, although rag.py show PATH:LINE -n N, facts, audit --entries and search --index exist. Some raw reads are legitimate: an agent editing an article must see its text, and kb-research reads external pages by line range. AGENTS.md already says deterministic tools first, and kb-lookup/SKILL.md follows it; nothing reaches an agent at the moment it types cat, since .claude/settings.json has no PreToolUse hook. Much of the census predates the current AGENTS.md wording, so repeat the census before building. Kb facts: public/claude/hooks.md:23 (PreToolUse permissionDecision and additionalContext, DOC S743), public/claude/hooks.md:70 (Bash matchers, DOC S743), public/claude/settings-and-scopes.md:75 (enforcement belongs in settings, not CLAUDE.md, DOC S1863).
